# SurfaceGuard 0.5.1

SurfaceGuard 0.5.1 is a defense-in-depth patch for hostile or ambiguous public build
artifacts.

URL inspection now recognizes uniformly, repeatedly, and mixed percent-encoded absolute
URLs within one shared decode budget while preserving exact raw source spans. Sitemap
parsing handles namespace-qualified locations, CDATA, comments, processing instructions,
and predefined or numeric XML entities in one forward pass. `DOCTYPE` declarations fail
closed because custom and external entities are not expanded.

Robots reconciliation preserves reserved percent octets and applies RFC 9309-style
prefix, wildcard, end-anchor, and path-plus-query matching. Separate ceilings bound
retained directives, route-by-rule comparisons, and total characters examined. Only the
exact root lowercase `robots.txt` is authoritative.

Automatic adapter selection now rejects conflicting strong signals instead of guessing.
The Next.js adapter recognizes `app-path-routes-manifest.json` and validates known
manifest containers and route fields. Valid extensionless text is inspected; ambiguous
unknown content fails closed when explicitly scoped or still predominantly textual,
without turning ordinary binary assets into text failures.

Policy validation eagerly rejects invalid globs and regular expressions, obvious nested
quantifiers, duplicate values, unsafe integers, and output fields beyond their declared
limits. The starter policy now denies both the exact `/staff` route and its descendants.
Zero-width decoded regex matches retain exact empty evidence and raw boundaries, and
JavaScript code-point escapes participate in bounded matching.

Retained evidence and messages, Markdown summaries, Action annotations, and SARIF paths
now have independent output boundaries. Truncated evidence includes its original UTF-8
size and SHA-256 digest, and report completeness distinguishes finding-row, evidence, and
text-inspection limits. New exported completeness and robots-limit fields are optional so
existing 0.5.0 TypeScript fixtures remain source-compatible.

Release automation now stages the notes and package archive together in a draft so
publication exposes both at the same time.

The attached package is for direct GitHub installation. This release is not published to
npm or another package registry.
